newsitem.title: USA: Crowley sees '96 net topping $1.6 million.
newsitem.headline: Crowley sees '96 net topping $1.6 million.

text.p: Crowley, Milner & Co president Denny Callahan said on Wednesday the company expects to report consolidated net earnings for 1996 of more than $1.6 million.
This is the highest earnings level the company has reported since 1987, and is an almost $4 million turnaround from the $2.3 million loss the company incurred last year, Callahan said in a statement.
Consolidated sales, including those from Steinbach stores since their acquisition at the end of August, 1996, approached $155 million, Callahan noted.
In 1995, the retailer reported sales of $105.9 million.

If sales from the Steinbach stores had been consolidated for the full year, total sales for the company would have approached the $200 million mark -- a target Callahan said the company expects to exceed in 1997.

Crowley's same-store sales for the year of more than $107 million represents a slight increase over the prior year's reported sales. The Steinbach stores have reported approximately $46 million in sales since the acquisition by Crowley's.
